title: Cadences
summary: Choose chords for cadences and recognise perfect, plagal and imperfect cadences.

provenance.notes: Items drawn from the seeded generators with a teaching-point filter, then fixed. Music and answers come from the rule engine; prompts and feedback are original.

items.prompt: Choose a chord for each marked melody note (A and B) in G major so that A–B makes a cadence. Each chord must contain its melody note.

music.textAlternative: A two-note melody in G major: A is A, B is G.

hints: List the chords containing each melody note.
A cadence ends on I or V.
List the chords that contain each melody note, then look for a pair that makes V–I, IV–I or ends on V.

feedback.correct: A good choice: both chords contain their melody notes and make a perfect cadence.

mistakes.chord-lacks-melody-note: The chord must include the melody note above it. Check the notes of the chord you chose.
mistakes.non-cadential-pair: Those two chords don't make one of the cadences. A cadence ends on chord I or chord V.
mistakes.cadence-misnamed: Look at the second chord: ending on V makes an imperfect cadence; V–I is perfect; IV–I is plagal.
mistakes.wrong-key: Check the key signature and the final note — then build the chords in that key.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. For each marked note, list the chords that contain it, then choose a pair that makes a cadence.
